key_insight: UniX resolves the tension between semantic understanding and pixel-level generation by combining autoregressive and diffusion capabilities in a unified foundation model for chest X-rays, avoiding the compromises of parameter-shared designs.
problem_solved: Addresses the conflict between semantic abstraction (diagnosis/analysis) and pixel-perfect reconstruction (image generation) in medical models, which causes degraded performance when using shared autoregressive architectures.
method: Hybrid dual-path architecture: an autoregressive pathway for semantic/clinical understanding and a diffusion pathway for high-fidelity image generation.
Decoupled parameterization with coordinated cross-module interaction to prevent one task from degrading the other.
Training strategy that balances abstraction and reconstruction objectives (e.g., staged or multi-task optimization) to align both capabilities in one foundation model.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners build medical foundation models that simultaneously deliver accurate chest X-ray interpretation and realistic image synthesis, improving downstream tasks like report generation, data augmentation, and robustness testing.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing dual autoregressive and diffusion pathways with coordination connections

paper_title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
